counterexamples.finding: No hidden reward/probabilistic preference model still assumes deterministic reflexive transitive preferences, finite explicitly available trajectory relation and distributions; cycles/statistical elicitation outside scope. Width-based compatible utility heuristic is exact compatibility but dimension not minimal, polynomial in |T| not necessarily SAH. Partial-order dominance hardness is conjectured; minimum utility dimension NP-hard is a different proved problem.

Fixed endpoint0/1 and epsilon gaps need epsilon≤1/(|T|-1) feasibility. B has stagewise column-sum dependencies for H≥2, so footnote claiming full column rank and (B^T B)^-1 needs pseudoinverse or gauge fixing. Do not silently change authors’ displayed expression or present it as general executable guarantee.

4.1(ii) coordinate utilities can tie without identical trajectories, so conversion to unique total orders needs tie handling. 5.1 step utility is only weakly monotone rather than strictly compatible, and tail sum need not be strictly negative; summation-by-parts argument requires care. 6.1 removes a sum of positive component-wise utility differences based on Pareto optimality; Pareto optimality alone does not make that sum nonpositive. Treat as unresolved proof-step questions, not certified theorem validity or venue guidance.

Potential RLHF applications are future relevance, not measured LLM improvement or statistical-efficient learning algorithm. No invented empirical section or removal of evidence-matched foundational language. Generic impact text is author choice, not automatically suitable for all applications.
